response: As I sit here on my [birthday] alone, I'm struck by the realization that I've spent most of my life carrying the weight of family expectations on my own shoulders. Growing up as an only child, I never had to navigate the complexities of sibling relationships or share the burden of household responsibilities with anyone else. (This has led to a unique dynamic where I often find myself relying on myself to get things done, whether it's [chores, emotional labor, or personal growth].) But as I've grown older, I've come to understand that this self-reliance has also made me more aware of the importance of quiet, intimate moments with loved ones. (Like the countless dinners I've shared with my parents, where we've had the space to talk about our hopes and fears, and I've learned to appreciate the value of deep, meaningful connections.) Yet, as I've entered adulthood, I've also begun to realize that this self-reliance can be a double-edged sword. (It's allowed me to develop a strong sense of independence, but it's also meant that I've had to carry the weight of family expectations alone, without anyone to share the burden with.) This has led to a sense of isolation, where I feel like I'm shouldering the responsibility of keeping everyone else happy, while also trying to figure out my own path in life. (It's a heavy burden to carry, and one that I'm still learning to navigate.) As I look back on my life, I'm starting to see that being an only child has shaped my approach to life's challenges and relationships in profound ways. (I've learned to be self-sufficient, but also to crave connection and intimacy with others.) And as I move forward, I'm determined to find a balance between my need for independence and my desire for meaningful relationships.
